[[Image:PaulMaurice2024.png|thumb|right|Paul Maurice has been head coach since 2022]]
The [[Florida Panthers]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in the [[Miami metropolitan area]]. They play in the [[Atlantic Division (NHL)|Atlantic Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL). The team joined the NHL in 1993 as an [[expansion team]], and won their first Eastern Conference championship in 1996. The Panthers have played their home games at the [[Amerant Bank Arena]] since 1998.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.thebbtcenter.com/about/history|title=History of the BB&T Center|publisher=BB&T Center|access-date=2012-12-16|archive-date=2023-04-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230404224205/http://www.thebbtcenter.com/about/history|url-status=live}}</ref> The Panthers are owned by Sunrise Sports and Entertainment, and [[Bill Zito]] is their [[general manager]].<ref name="martin"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://panthers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=Panthers_FrontOffice|title=Florida Panthers - Front Office|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|access-date=2008-12-05|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090307052802/http://panthers.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&bcid=Panthers_FrontOffice|archive-date=2009-03-07}}</ref>

There have been 16&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Panthers franchise. The team's first head coach was [[Roger Neilson]], who coached for two complete seasons from 1993 to 1995.<ref name="neilson"/> The Panther's current head coach is [[Paul Maurice]].

==Notes==
* {{note label|Note1|a|a}} A running total of the number of coaches of the Panthers. Thus, any coach who has two or more separate terms as head coach is only counted once.
* {{note label|Note2|b|b}} Before the 2005–06 season, the NHL instituted a [[Overtime (ice hockey)#Shootout|penalty shootout]] for regular season games that remained tied after a five-minute overtime period, which prevented ties.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511234846/http://www.nhl.com/ext/0708rules.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=2008-05-11|title=Official Rules|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|access-date=2008-12-05}}</ref>
* {{note label|Note3|c|c}} In hockey, the winning percentage is calculated by dividing points by maximum possible [[Point (ice hockey)|points]].
* {{note label|Note4|d|d}} Each year is linked to an article about that particular NHL season.
*{{note label|Note5|e|e}} Includes the Qualifying Round of the [[2020 Stanley Cup playoffs]].
